hints.content:
###The strategy

The perimeter of a quadrilateral is the sum of the lengths of all the sides. 

Side $\overline{CD}$ is perfectly horizontal, so we can find its length using the $x$-coordinates of its endpoints.

We can find the length of $\overline{AB}$, $\overline{BC}$, and $\overline{DA}$ using the Pythagorean theorem (or the distance formula).

###Step 1: Finding the length $AB$



[[☃ image 1]]

$\begin{align} AB^2&= {\redE{9}^2 +\redE{4}^2 } &&\text{Pythagorean theorem} \\\\
AB&= \sqrt{\redE{9}^2 +\redE{4}^2 } &&\text{Square root both sides}\\\\
&=\tealE{\sqrt{97}}
\end{align}$

options.alt: A coordinate plane. Quadrilateral A B C D has point A at negative three, two, point B at six, negative two, point C at three, negative six, and point D at zero, negative six. A highlighted horizontal line of nine units connects from point A to a highlighted vertical line of four units to point B.

hints.content:
###Step 2: Finding the length $BC$



[[☃ image 1]]

$\begin{align} 
BC^2&= \redE{3}^2 +\redE{4}^2  &&\text{Pythagorean theorem} \\\\
BC&= \sqrt{\redE{3}^2 +\redE{4}^2 }   &&\text{Square root both sides} \\\\
&=\sqrt{25} \\\\
&=\goldE{5}
\end{align}$

options.alt: A coordinate plane. Quadrilateral A B C D has point A at negative three, two, point B at six, negative two, point C at three, negative six, and point D at zero, negative six. A highlighted horizontal line of three units connects from point C to a highlighted vertical line of four units to point B.

hints.content:
###Step 3: Finding the length $DA$



[[☃ image 1]]

$\begin{align} 
DA^2&= \redE{3}^2 +\redE{8}^2  &&\text{Pythagorean theorem} \\\\
DA&= \sqrt{\redE{3}^2 +\redE{8}^2 }   &&\text{Square root both sides} \\\\
&=\purpleD{\sqrt{73}}
\end{align}$

options.alt: A coordinate plane. Quadrilateral A B C D has point A at negative three, two, point B at six, negative two, point C at three, negative six, and point D at zero, negative six. A highlighted horizontal line of three units connects from point D to a highlighted vertical line of eight units to point A.

hints.content:
###Step 4: Finding the perimeter

Side $\overline{CD}$ is perfectly horizontal, so we can use the $x$-coordinates of its endpoints to see that this side is $3$ units long.

Using the lengths of all $4$ sides, we can find the perimeter of quadrilateral $ABCD$:

$\begin{align} \text{Perimeter} &= AB+BC+CD+DA \\\\
&=\tealE{\sqrt{97}}+\goldE{5}+3+\purpleD{\sqrt{73}} \\\\
&= 8+\sqrt{97}+\sqrt{73}
\end{align}$

###The answer

The exact perimeter of quadrilateral $ABCD$ is $8+\sqrt{97}+\sqrt{73}$ units (approximately $26.4$ units).
